 Usman Khawaja, David Warner dropped from commentary duties after Sandpapergate storm
 Usman Khawaja and David Warner have been stood down from Fox Cricket commentary duties amid the fresh Sandpapergate controversy. The decision comes after renewed allegations about Australia's 2018 ball-tampering scandal.
 Advertisement Khawaja and Warner have been made to step down from their commentary duties (Courtesy: Getty) By: India Today Sports Desk Nov 21, 2026 12:43 IST Last Updated Nov 21, 2026 12:43 IST Published by alan john Nov 21, 2026 12:43 IST The sandpapergate storm has hit the Australian shores hard over the past few weeks and it has come at a price for Usman Khawaja and David Warner. The former Aussie opening duo have been removed from their Fox Cricket commentary duties until the storm dies down.
 With the Sandpapergate controversy showing no signs of dying down , Fox Sports has opted to remove the two commentators from the spotlight, believing it is the best course of action for both amid the ongoing fallout.
 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story “In light of recent events, both Usman and Davey will be rested from our broadcasts over the next few weeks,’’ Fox Sports managing director Steve Crawley told CODE Sports.
 “While we always support all members of our commentary team and welcome a diversity of views which is a feature of our summer of cricket we also understand the pressure they are under to respond to each and every new comment."
 “We think it is increasingly difficult to focus on the game while the situation continues to unfold and think it is unfair on both commentators to put them in that position.
 “Our focus remains on providing our viewers with the best broadcast of Australia’s summer of cricket. We will continue to monitor the situation.’’
 A return date for Khawaja and Warner to commentary hasn't been set at this point in time.
 SANDPAPERGATE GETS REIGNITED
 The Sandpapergate debate returned to the spotlight after Usman Khawaja's autobiography, Sabr, claimed that knowledge of the ball-tampering plan went beyond Cameron Bancroft, Steve Smith and David Warner. Pat Cummins rejected the suggestion, describing claims that the entire team knew about the sandpaper plot as "complete and utter nonsense".
 Bancroft subsequently added fuel to the controversy, alleging that the wider squad was aware of the practice and that bowlers, including Cummins, had discussed the ball's condition. He said Cummins' press conference was the "final straw" that pushed him to break his silence.
 Despite fans and critics feeling that Pat Cummins' captaincy reign won't survive the storm, Cricket Australia has backed the pacer to remain in charge of the side.
 Cummins has received support from Josh Hazlewood, who said that there would be a mutiny if the current Australian skipper is forced to quit from his role. - Ends Tune In Must Watch
